page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the instance supplies 8 virtual CPUs mapped across 4 physical cores via multithreading. It features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by standard hardware encryption extensions including AES and SHA-NI.

Hardware allocations deliver a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, totaling 64 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates 1600 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core CPU throughput on stress-ng, alongside strong memory subsystem performance. Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 258.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 152.63 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. In contrast, multi-core processing, static web serving, and integer compression benchmarks place in the average range. LLM inference shows limitations under higher parameter demands, recording lower-tier prompt processing speeds on medium 7B models.

The dense pairing of 64 GB RAM with 1600 GB fast local NVMe storage offers strong operational efficiency for I/O and data-intensive tasks without incurring external block storage overhead. The configuration is directly aligned with memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and NoSQL database management, and intensive extract, transform, load pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-1600s-amd is a memory-oriented server in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, powered by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores, paired with 64 GB of system RAM for an 8:1 memory-to-core density. Storage is handled locally by an integrated 1600 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional stress-ng single-core compute performance and strong large-block memory bandwidth exceeding 258 GB/sec for reads. While multi-threaded compute and language model prompt processing exhibit moderate to low throughput, the high RAM allocation and direct-attached NVMe disk deliver balanced resource efficiency for memory-constrained and I/O-sensitive applications. It is tailored for production relational databases, Redis key-value caching stores, data transformation, and medium-scale backend analytics.
